question:
Consider the function $f(x)=\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-1}{2}\right)$.

(a) Determine the domain of $f$.

(b) Determine the range of $f$.

(c) Find all values of $x$ for which $f(x)=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, and verify that the obtained values belong to the domain.
explanation:
(a)
For $\sec^{-1}t$ to be defined, $|t|\geq1$. Therefore,
$$\left|\frac{x-1}{2}\right|\geq1$$
$$|x-1|\geq2$$
Hence,
$$x-1\leq-2\quad\text{or}\quad x-1\geq2$$
Thus,
$$x\leq-1\quad\text{or}\quad x\geq3$$
Therefore, the domain is
$$(-\infty,-1]\cup[3,\infty)$$

(b)
The principal-value range of $\sec^{-1}t$ is
$$[0,\pi]-\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$$
Therefore, the range of $f$ is
$$\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\pi\right]$$

(c)
Given that
$$\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{x-1}{2}\right)=\frac{2\pi}{3}$$
taking secant on both sides gives
$$\frac{x-1}{2}=\sec\frac{2\pi}{3}=-2$$
Therefore,
$$x-1=-4$$
$$x=-3$$
Since $-3\leq-1$, the obtained value belongs to the domain. Hence, the required value is $x=-3$.
